description: Proposed alert rules for Temperature, Action (flow) and Concentration (conductivity). Derived from the July 2026 CIP logs; NOT approved by Danone. See docs/TACT_rules_proposal.md. Loaded by cip_alerting/proposed_rules.py; CIP_PROPOSED_RULES=off|show|alert (default show: panel only, no alerts).
basis: CIP logs 1–26 Jul 2026, 4 CIP lines, 38,943 readings; objects with reference thresholds only

conditions.below_set_point_minus: reading < set point - thresholds.belowBy (unit of the signal)
conditions.common: Checked during the rule's step only. The first thresholds.graceMinutes of each continuous block of that step are not checked (ramp-up allowance). Met when consecutive valid readings stay below the limit for thresholds.minutes or longer (first to latest reading). Missing readings, readings outside the plausible sensor range, a reading at or above the limit, or a change of step end the streak. One alert per rule per cycle.

rules.title: Caustic wash temperature low
rules.rationale: Return temperature reaches the 80 °C set point within 3 min of circulation in 90% of runs (median 1 min) and then sits a median 9.9 °C above it; after the first 5 min only 3.5% of readings are more than 5 °C below. A 5 min streak more than 5 °C below therefore stands out from normal ramp-up and sensor noise.

rules.title: Acid wash temperature low
rules.rationale: Same shape as the caustic rule: the 65 °C set point is reached within 4 min in 90% of runs and the median reading is 15.4 °C above it. Using one temperature rule for both chemical washes keeps it simple to explain.

rules.title: Caustic concentration low
rules.rationale: Return conductivity is above the 55 mS/cm set point from the first minute in 90% of runs (median 164% of set point); only 1.8% of readings after the first 5 min are below 90% of it. 90% matches the 10% tolerance the monitor already uses for time and flow.

rules.title: Acid concentration low
rules.rationale: Unlike caustic, acid conductivity runs close to its 65 mS/cm set point (median 99%) and 52% of readings after the first 5 min are below it, so a 'below set point' rule would be noisy. 90% of set point keeps the same tolerance as the other rules; the alerts it projects come from long streaks (median 62 min). Needs confirmation that 65 mS/cm is the intended acid set point.

rules.title: Caustic wash flow low
rules.rationale: The PLC's own Min Return Flow SP is a minimum, and the monitor already flags median flow below 90% of reference. Return flow is at or above the minimum in 75% of readings after the first 5 min, but 18% are below 90% of it; requiring 5 min in a row ignores short dips. 8% of readings are negative (outside the plausible range) and are not counted.

rules.title: Acid wash flow low
rules.rationale: Same rule as caustic flow. It projects no alerts on the July data because 29% of acid circulation flow readings are negative (outside the plausible range) and break every low-flow streak; counting them as zero flow would give 10 alerts. Kept so that Danone can decide how negative readings should be treated.

rules.title: Pre-rinse flow low
rules.rationale: Rinse circulation is short (median 2 min, 90% under 7 min), so the chemical-wash timing (5 + 5 min) would almost never apply. A 2 min ramp-up allowance and a 3 min streak cover the rinses that circulate long enough to judge.

rules.title: Mid rinse flow low
rules.rationale: Same rinse timing as pre-rinse (mid-rinse circulation: median 5 min). Mid rinse has no time limit in the reference workbook, so this would be its only check.

rules.title: Final rinse flow low
rules.rationale: Same rinse timing as pre-rinse (final-rinse circulation: median 4 min).
